children: Friedman Industries, Incorporated

FRD investors have been experiencing some short-term gains from the stock of late. Shares of the Longview, TX-based diversified metals processing and pipe manufacturer have gained 83.9% in the past three months against the industry’s 13.9% decline. The stock also outperformed the sector and the S&P 500’s 1.8% and 0.6% gains, respectively, in the same time frame.

A major development of FRD in recent months includes the announcement of its promising first-quarter fiscal 2027 results in August. In the fiscal first quarter, the company reported higher sales, driven by record sales volumes, stronger customer demand, improved average selling prices, increased capacity utilization across existing facilities and contributions from the Century Metals acquisition. Most of the year-over-year volume growth came from existing operations. Friedman operates through two reportable segments — flat-roll products and tubular products. The flat-roll segment benefited from higher volumes, stronger pricing and the acquisition, while the tubular segment also delivered improved sales and operating performance.

Management highlighted that Century Metals continues to contribute to growth and profitability while expanding Friedman’s geographic reach and customer offering. It also emphasized the strength of its commercial strategy and efforts to improve capacity utilization and deepen customer relationships. Looking ahead, the company expects second-quarter fiscal 2027 sales volumes to remain comparable with the fiscal first quarter and anticipates sequential margin improvement supported by higher average selling prices.
FRD’s Three Months Price Comparison
Over the past three months, the stock’s performance has remained strong, outperforming that of its peers like
NN, Inc.
NNBR and
TechPrecision Corporation
TPCS. NN and TechPrecision’s shares have gained 8.9% and 45.3%, respectively, in the same time frame.
Despite cyclical and volatile steel market conditions, the favorable share price movement suggests FRD is well-positioned to sustain its positive momentum at present.

Friedman’s flat-roll products segment primarily generates revenues from the sale of company-owned inventory, while also generating revenues by processing and storing customer-owned material on a fee basis. The tubular products segment generates revenues from the sale of company-owned inventory.
FRD’s Operational Growth Drivers

Value-added services and internal efficiencies offer another avenue for growth. Friedman is focused on improving gross margins through operating efficiencies and expanding value-added services. Its broad processing capabilities, including cut-to-length, slitting and other specialized processing, allow FRD to address varied customer requirements and extract greater value from its operating platform.

Capacity expansion provides FRD with additional room for growth. Over the past several years, the company has expanded its operating platform through the PlatePlus facilities, the greenfield Sinton operation and a second Granite City processing facility. Management sees further scope to grow volumes toward available capacity and improve efficiency using its existing assets.

Customer and product diversification further supports FRD’s prospects. The company highlights longstanding relationships with major customers and a favorable geographic footprint that provides cost-efficient access to customers. Its diverse offering includes ferrous and non-ferrous products, while technological capabilities help support customer loyalty.
Friedman’s Strategic Strengths

The Century Metals acquisition has expanded FRD’s growth opportunities. The transaction broadened the company’s geographic reach, customer offering and flat-roll processing capabilities. Century Metals has integrated well into Friedman’s platform and is contributing to growth and profitability, demonstrating the company’s ability to supplement its organic expansion through acquisitions.

Risk management and capital discipline provide support amid cyclical metals markets. Friedman uses derivatives to manage price-cycle risks and protect inventory value, while also improving purchasing flexibility and capital efficiency. Its disciplined capital-allocation approach and balance-sheet strength provide additional flexibility to pursue growth opportunities while navigating commodity-price volatility.
Challenges Ahead for FRD

Steel price volatility remains a key challenge for FRD, as sharp price movements can affect inventory values, selling prices and margins, while also influencing customer purchasing patterns. Although Friedman uses derivatives to mitigate price-cycle risks, hedging cannot eliminate this exposure. Demand cyclicality is another concern, as metals markets are inherently cyclical, making sales volumes and capacity utilization vulnerable to shifts in steel demand, economic activity and conditions across the end markets the company serves.
Friedman Stock’s Valuation
Friedman’s trailing 12-month EV/Sales of 0.4X is lower than the industry’s average of 1.9X but higher than its five-year median of 0.2X.
NN and TechPrecision’s trailing 12-month EV/Sales currently stand at 1.2X and 1.7X, respectively, in the same time frame.
Our Final Take on FRD

Friedman’s strong share-price momentum appears to have a fundamental foundation. The company is benefiting from improved utilization of its operating platform, capacity expansion, value-added processing capabilities and a broader customer and product base. The successful integration of Century Metals further strengthens its geographic reach and processing capabilities, while disciplined risk management provides support through changing market conditions.

However, sustaining the rally will depend on Friedman’s ability to execute consistently through steel-industry cycles. Steel price volatility can affect margins, inventory values and customer purchasing behavior, while fluctuations in end-market demand could influence volumes and capacity utilization. FRD’s hedging practices help mitigate some price-cycle risks but cannot eliminate the inherent cyclicality of the business.

From a valuation standpoint, FRD still appears reasonably positioned despite its sharp run-up, suggesting that improving fundamentals could support additional upside if the company continues executing its growth strategy. However, the stock’s valuation has become less conservative following the rally, indicating that some optimism surrounding Friedman’s improved business prospects is already reflected in the share price. As a result, further appreciation is likely to depend increasingly on sustained operational progress and earnings delivery rather than a simple re-rating of the stock.

For existing shareholders, the combination of organic growth opportunities, available capacity, acquisition benefits and disciplined execution supports staying invested. Prospective investors may also find FRD worth considering, although the magnitude of the recent rally warrants some caution. The momentum has scope to continue, but maintaining it will require Friedman to capitalize on its growth opportunities while effectively navigating steel-price and demand cycles.
